blogs.title: Beyond the 5-Day Rule: Recognizing Early-Onset HIT After Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: This post challenges the conventional 'POD 5-10' timeline for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) in cardiac surgery patients. We analyze a case where rapid thrombocytopenia (<5 days) was driven by pre-operative heparin exposure during cardiac catheterization. The discussion focuses on refining the clinical suspicion for HIT when platelet counts drop earlier than expected, emphasizing that recent heparin exposure—even days prior to surgery—can precipitate severe, early-onset autoimmune HIT.

blogs.title: When the Serotonin Release Assay Lies: Decoding Atypical Autoimmune HIT Profiles
blogs.description: Standard HIT diagnostics rely heavily on the Serotonin Release Assay (SRA), yet this case presents a unique 'indeterminate' profile characterized by strong platelet activation in the *absence* of heparin and partial resistance to Fc-receptor blocking antibodies. We dissect this novel serological phenotype, explaining why traditional interpretation algorithms might fail and how recognizing heparin-independent platelet activation is critical for diagnosing severe autoimmune HIT (aHIT).

blogs.title: Refractory Thrombocytopenia: Why IVIG Sometimes Fails in Severe Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: High-dose Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) is often considered a first-line rescue therapy for autoimmune HIT to block pathogenic antibodies. However, this case illustrates a scenario where even massive doses of IVIG failed to produce the typical brisk platelet recovery. We explore the mechanisms behind refractory aHIT, discuss alternative management strategies like switching anticoagulants from argatroban to fondaparinux, and highlight markers of persistent hypercoagulability (falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimer) that signal treatment failure.

blogs.title: The Hidden Stroke: Navigating Neurological Complications in Post-Cardiac Surgery Thrombocytopenia
blogs.description: Thrombosis remains the greatest danger in HIT, yet neurological symptoms can be masked by post-operative delirium or sedation. This post examines a case of acute parietal stroke presenting solely as worsening confusion in a patient with dropping platelets. We discuss the diagnostic tension between attributing mental status changes to anesthesia/delirium versus occult thromboembolism and outline an algorithm for when to image the brain immediately upon detecting significant thrombocytopenia in the ICU setting.

blogs.title: Anticoagulation Dilemmas: Argatroban vs. Fondaparinux in Severe Post-Stroke Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Managing anticoagulation in a patient with active arterial thrombosis (stroke), profound thrombocytopenia (nadir 13k), and suspected HIT requires balancing bleeding risks against catastrophic clot propagation. We compare the pharmacokinetic profiles of argatroban and fondaparinux in this specific high-risk context, analyzing why a transition from continuous infusion to subcutaneous therapy was necessary despite initial concerns about renal clearance and anti-factor Xa monitoring.
